title: Finesse Router: spot-blend GPU hints and tenant throttles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a lightweight policy layer that chooses region/tier and GPU class while respecting per-tenant soft budget caps and minimizing SLO violations when using spot instances. Current router picks by static priority and often either over-commits spot capacity (leading to evictions) or falls back too eagerly to expensive on-demand GPUs.

Goal: Implement a 'Finesse Router' prototype that combines a preemption-probability score, GPU-class suitability hints from the runtime, and a tenant-facing soft-throttle that gradually degrades non-critical requests to quantized model variants when spend approaches a cap. The router should produce explainable decisions for debugging and tie into cost dashboards.

Out of scope for this ticket: billing pipeline changes, console UX polish, and deeply integrated ML-driven predictive models (we will use simple EWMA and heuristics for now).
acceptance_criteria: Router accepts per-request hints and evaluates region/tier/gpu choice in <8ms p95 in staging under synthetic traffic
When tenant spend window reaches 85% of soft cap, low-priority traffic is routed to a quantized model variant or optional batch queue with <5% SLO error increase
Spot preemption probability computed from recent eviction rate and instance-type volatility and used to avoid >10% extra latency compared to baseline when hedging
Decision logs contain structured fields: chosen_region, chosen_tier, chosen_gpu_class, fallback_variant, cost_estimate, decision_reason
Integration tests cover spot->on-demand fallback and GPU-class fallback with mocked capacity signals
Design doc and rollout plan reviewed by Runtime and Billing leads
tasks: Design: define decision inputs, scoring formula, and fields for decision log (Assignee: Marco, 2 pts)
Runtime: add GPU-class hint endpoint that returns suitability score per model variant (Assignee: Jordan Kim, 3 pts)
Router: implement EWMA-based spot preemption estimator and combine with tenant burn-rate to compute risk score (Assignee: Marco Li, 3 pts)
Policy: implement tenant soft-throttle that marks requests as 'degradeable' and routes them to cheaper variants when threshold crossed (Assignee: Aisha Patel, 2 pts)
Tests: add unit and integration tests simulating evictions and spend windows (Assignee: QA Team, 2 pts)
Observability: emit metrics and labels for decisions; add a debug endpoint to replay decisions (Assignee: Sophie Nguyen, 2 pts)
Docs: short PRD and API examples for SDK teams to pass 'degradeable' hint (Assignee: Marco Li, 1 pt)
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and gating metrics posted. Proposed scoring: risk = alpha*preempt_prob + beta*(burn_rate/soft_cap). Open questions: appropriate alpha/beta and how long EWMA window should be.

2026-03-04 - Marco Li: Implemented local prototype of preempt_prob EWMA (window 10m) and added synthetic load tests. Observed that p95 decision latency is ~6ms in Go router. Pushed branch for review: PR #482.
2026-03-06 - Jordan Kim: Added GPU-class hint endpoint in runtime with a simple compute-cost estimate and fidelity score. Need to standardize fidelity score across quantized variants.
2026-03-07 - Sophie Nguyen: Observability scaffold added: decision logs and metrics (router.decision.*). Will add Grafana dashboard tiles in a follow-up.
2026-03-09 - Security review request: Requested review of decision log contents; masking applied to tenant identifiers per SRE feedback.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Demo to PMs showed graceful degradation for non-critical traffic; product asked for an opt-out flag for specific endpoints. Added to tasks.
notes: Trade-offs: we prioritize predictable SLOs over absolute cost savings for critical traffic. Soft-throttle preserves UX by degrading lower-priority requests first. Future work could replace EWMA with ML forecasting and introduce an adaptive alpha/beta optimizer. Monitoring: track decision-reversal rate and any customer complaints tied to quantized degradations.
